binary.reason: Inherited from @thalovant/sdk, and now run rather than asserted: the shared vectors go through whatever version actually resolves here, which is the thing a dependency range never showed. This server implements none of the three itself -- it passes sessionId through to ask and exposes no tool of its own for the hive kinds or binary frames -- so what is on par is the SDK beneath it, and that is what these cases check. The frames decoded are hivemind-bus-client's own encoder output, vendored as binary-frames.json, so this is the wire a hub really puts out rather than bytes built here -- encodeHiveBinaryFrame refuses to build one, because re-encoding would drop binary.data.

mesh.reason: Inherited from @thalovant/sdk, and now run rather than asserted: the shared vectors go through whatever version actually resolves here, which is the thing a dependency range never showed. This server implements none of the three itself -- it passes sessionId through to ask and exposes no tool of its own for the hive kinds or binary frames -- so what is on par is the SDK beneath it, and that is what these cases check. refusal.reason: This server implements no part of an ask itself: it hands every turn to @thalovant/sdk, so the refusal behaviour arrives with the dependency. Being on par means running the shared vectors against the version that actually resolves here, as the other inherited capabilities do -- and @thalovant/sdk 0.8.2, which carries the rule and exports failureError/refusalBelongsToAsk, is not published yet. Planned rather than claimed: the range bump and the inherited-parity cases land the day it is, and --release refuses to publish over this until they do.

runtime.reason: Applicable public behavior is implemented and exercised by the named regression suites and shared fixtures. HiveMind #251/#252 only changes the Python upstream client dispatcher; this consumer uses native single-dispatch transports (MCP delegates to the Node SDK), or caller-owned frame parsing in embedded C. No Python HiveMind bus dependency or slave-protocol reinjection exists here. Python now requires fixed upstream 1.1.9a1 and removes its identity-based suppression; equal independent native frames remain distinct. Reply claim metadata follows the Python string-ID contract, with first-seen ordering, case-sensitive fallback stages and legacy unstamped success. Invalid non-string stamps are ignored. Embedded C exposes bounded extraction and claim classification while its caller retains ordered IDs.

session.reason: MCP runtime connections and identity leases are scoped to a tool invocation; persistent sockets and origin overrides are not exposed.
